Reduce the following radical equation into a simple linear equation then find its solution. In case of extraneous solution, write $\phi$ for the solution set.
$\sqrt{\frac{a+6}{a+2}}=\sqrt{\frac{a+2}{a-1}}$
keyPoints: ["Cross-multiply after squaring equal square roots","Reject values that empty any denominator"]
modelAnswer:
Squaring removes the radicals: $\frac{a+6}{a+2}=\frac{a+2}{a-1}$.
Cross-multiplying: $(a+6)(a-1)=(a+2)^{2}$, so $a^{2}+5a-6=a^{2}+4a+4$, giving $a=10$.
Checking $a \neq -2, 1$: valid. Solution set $\{10\}$.

Reduce the following radical equation into a simple linear equation then find its solution. In case of extraneous solution, write $\phi$ for the solution set.
$\sqrt{\frac{z}{z+3}}=\sqrt{\frac{z+2}{z+6}}$
keyPoints: ["Quadratic terms cancel to a linear equation"]
modelAnswer:
$\frac{z}{z+3}=\frac{z+2}{z+6}$ after squaring.
Cross-multiplying: $z(z+6)=(z+2)(z+3)$, so $z^{2}+6z=z^{2}+5z+6$, giving $z=6$.
Solution set $\{6\}$.
